newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA STRUGGLE IN FIRST SESSION.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA STRUGGLE IN FIRST SESSION.

text.p: Dean Headley celebrated his test debut with a wicket from his 18th delivery as Australia struggled to 78 for three by lunch on the first day of the third test at Old Trafford on Thursday.
Batting was hard work as England's seamers gained plenty of movement and frequently beat the bat.
But opener Matthew Elliott gradually began to play his shots and was unbeaten on 36 by the interval, having added 36 with Steve Waugh (19) after Australia had earlier been reduced to 42 for three.

Australian captain Mark Taylor had a difficult decision after winning the toss on an overcast morning. The pitch was damp, with bare patches as well as some green ones, and seemed likely to favour bowlers rather than batsmen from the start.
Taylor elected to bat and found himself back in the pavilion after facing 20 balls and making only two.
Headley, selected ahead of Mike Smith and Devon Malcolm, made the initial breakthrough for England when he induced Taylor to edge a catch to first slip where Graham Thorpe took a good, low catch.
It was the third time in four innings in the series that Taylor had been dismissed for single figures, the other having brought a century at Edgbaston when his place was on the line.
Neither Greg Blewett nor Mark Waugh found batting any easier. Blewett played on to Darren Gough for eight, trying to cut, and Waugh gave Alec Stewart a catch behind the wicket for 12 off Alan Ealham.
Ealham might have added the wicket of Elliott in his second over when the opener edged him just wide of slip.
